newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO waiting for briefing, unimpressed by summit.
newsitem.headline: PLO waiting for briefing, unimpressed by summit.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak's adviser will brief Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Wednesday on results of the Israeli-Egyptian summit which appeared to leave PLO officials unimpressed.
Osama al-Baz is due in Gaza a day after Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a bid to revive stalled Israel-PLO peace talks.
The two leaders made no breakthroughs but said their summit in Egypt resort town of Sharm el-Sheikh would be followed by further talks on obstacles in the peace process.

"We had said before the summit there would be no dramatic breakthrough but a first step towards resuming negotiations and I think the first step was taken," said Netanyahu's media adviser David Bar-Illan after returning to Israel.
Asked when Israel and the PLO would renew talks halted after Israeli bulldozers broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem two months ago, Bar-Illan said:
"I'd rather not venture any specific prediction on this but we do expect it soon."
Palestinians were less upbeat. An aide to Arafat said the summit had not eased the crisis in Middle East peacemaking.
Asked if the meeting between the two leaders brought about an improvement in the situation, Ahmed Tibi said: "Not at all."
"There was no commitment to halt settlements... there is no change in the substance of the main issues," he told Israel's Channel Two television.
A settlement freeze is Arafat's condition for resuming talks with Israel but Netanyahu rules out any halt in West Bank construction for Jews.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Cairo would wait to receive Netanyahu's response to issues raised at the summit before al-Baz shuttles between Israel and the Palestinians.
"We need to hear from the Israeli side about the issues raised by the president," he told Israel Radio's English service in a phone interview.
A PLO official said al-Baz would meet Arafat in Gaza at 10 a.m. (0700 GMT).
Mubarak said after the summit that he had discussed the issue of settlements with Netanyahu but they agreed any solution needed more talks.

"We exchanged views concerning the settlements and we are still going to have more discussions so as to put the key in the door and open it," Mubarak told a news conference in which the two men joked and appeared relaxed.
"We need another meeting and we need more deliberation."

Asked if the further deliberations would include the Palestinians, Mubarak said: "We intend as far as we can to bring the main partner in(to) the meeting but this depends on so many elements. We hope that we could conclude it in the next meeting and then after that the third element could come."
Netanyahu referred to the meeting with Mubarak as a "positive beginning. But we need more work and we are committed to work together with you (Egypt) to achieve progress".
"This was a first step and a first step means there are more steps," Netanyahu said. "In no circumstances would I characterise what went on here today as a failure."
